edits.new: The appraisal document of 13 February 2012 prints one legal covenant and no condition of effectiveness or disbursement. The covenant binds the borrower, through the Ministry of Railways, to implement the project and to make the provinces implement it in accordance with the safeguards instruments, in a manner and substance satisfactory to the Bank, and to monitor those instruments every six months. The project was Environmental Category A, and four safeguard policies were triggered: environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01), natural habitats (OP/BP 4.04), physical cultural resources (OP/BP 4.11) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). OP 4.12 was triggered because the project takes land, so a resettlement action plan, a resettlement policy framework and a social assessment were prepared. The project company prepared the plan and the framework, both acceptable to the Bank, and the covenant is what makes them binding. The plan sets out how grievances are to be handled, how resettlement is to be monitored inside and outside the project, who implements it and where the money for it comes from. It was disclosed in China on 4 January 2012. Procurement plans and any change to them had to go to the Bank for prior review and no objection before use.

The appraisal document of 14 April 2010 lists the loan's conditions and covenants and leaves the line for effectiveness conditions blank. The loan had to be passed down in a fixed way: the borrower on-lent it to Anhui province and Anhui to Anqing, Huaibei, Lu'an and Wuhu on the same terms, with the municipalities carrying the currency risk. Anhui and the four cities had to keep an adequate organisational structure in place. Anhui had to make each city carry out its resettlement action plan and environmental management plan, prepare and carry out annual work plans, hire consultants to supervise the works, and hire consultants to monitor how the resettlement and environmental plans were being carried out, send the Bank the results every six months and act on their recommendations. Anhui also owed six-monthly project reports and a mid-term report by 15 August 2013. The project was Environmental Category B. The appraisal data sheet names two triggered safeguard policies, environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12); the completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review name those two and physical cultural resources (OP 4.11).

The appraisal document of 28 May 2004 sets out a single condition of effectiveness, and it is about resettlement: a legal opinion confirming that the resettlement arrangements between the Ministry of Railways and each of the provinces of Hunan, Jiangxi and Zhejiang, entered into to cause the resettlement action plan to be carried out, were legally binding on the parties. Until that opinion was given the loan could not become effective. The ministry then had standing obligations: to take all necessary actions to minimise as far as possible any involuntary loss by people of shelter, productive assets, access to productive assets, income or means of livelihood, temporary or permanent; to carry out the environmental management plan, the resettlement plan and those arrangements in a manner satisfactory to the Bank; and to send any proposed change to the three to the Bank for approval. Other covenants were about the railway: power supply agreements by 1 August 2006, a timetable for the new trains by 31 December 2004, operating rules by 1 August 2006, and twice-yearly financial monitoring reports with yearly reports of results. The technical assistance carried its own terms: studies under terms of reference acceptable to the Bank, the studies' recommendations to the Bank by 15 February each year, action plans for them by 31 July each year, and those action plans carried out. The project was Environmental Category A, and the data sheet names environmental assessment (OP/BP/GP 4.01) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12) as the triggered policies.

The appraisal document of 20 May 2013 prints one condition of effectiveness and six legal covenants. The condition was that a subsidiary agreement be executed between the project implementing entity, Nanchang Municipality and the Urban Rail Company. The covenants required the implementing entity to keep an organisational structure satisfactory to the Bank, including a Project Leading Group to oversee the work and a Project Management Office to run it; to carry out the Integration Plan as approved, or as adjusted in consultation with the Bank; to make the municipality and the rail company carry out the safeguards instruments in a manner and substance satisfactory to the Bank; and to furnish six-monthly project reports by 31 March and 30 September, half-yearly interim financial reports and audited financial statements within six months of each year's end. The project was Environmental Category A, and environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01), physical cultural resources (OP 4.11) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12) were triggered. Under OP 4.12 the project office prepared a resettlement action plan, following Chinese law as well as the policy, with a resettlement policy framework for parts of the works that might move, and both were disclosed. The safeguards covenant covers the demolition work whoever paid for it.

The appraisal document of 30 May 2006 sets out two conditions of effectiveness: eight subsidiary loan agreements, satisfactory to the Bank, signed between the project counties and their water utility companies; and financial management training given to all staff responsible for implementation, a condition to be dropped if Henan showed before signing that it was already done. A disbursement covenant made spending under a subproject eligible only where that county's subsidiary loan agreement was signed and a legal opinion confirmed it. Other covenants: Bank review of five competitive bidding contracts before the bid documents were finished in the first year, and two of each in later years; improvement action plans for the low-performing water companies by 31 December 2006; remedial works at Longxingsi reservoir in Baofeng county and Boshan reservoir in Queshan county, with operating and monitoring procedures in place by 31 December 2006; and a financial covenant requiring each water company to earn revenues at least equal to its operating expenses plus the excess of debt service over depreciation plus its own capital spending. The conformed Project Agreement for loan 4829-CN carries the land obligations. Henan, the counties and the water companies had to minimise involuntary loss of shelter, productive assets, access to them, income or livelihood, and for that purpose had to implement the resettlement action plan in a manner satisfactory to the Bank before any works began. Any change to or waiver of that plan needed the Bank's prior agreement. Independent monitoring agencies acceptable to the Bank had to be engaged, and six-monthly reports on monitoring the environmental plan, dam safety and the resettlement plan were due to the Bank by 30 March and 30 September each year from 2007. The subsidiary loan agreements themselves had to make each water company undertake to implement its part of the works in accordance with the resettlement plan and the environmental plan. The completion report records the six-monthly reporting covenant as only partially complied with, and a covenant to prepare a plan for continued achievement of the project's objectives by 31 December 2013 as not complied with. Those tables list four covenants of the whole schedule.

The appraisal document of 20 January 2012 prints thirteen conditions and legal covenants, all under the project agreement with Sichuan, and no condition of effectiveness. Sichuan had to keep the project's leading groups and project offices in place to 31 December 2017. It had to apply the project implementation plan, the resettlement action plan, the environmental management plan, the pest management plan, the annual implementation plan and the annual dam safety action plan in a manner satisfactory to the Bank, and could not amend, suspend or waive any of them without the Bank's prior agreement. Two covenants went directly to the people moved: Sichuan had to carry out measures satisfactory to the Bank for improving the living standard of displaced persons in accordance with the resettlement plan, and had to hire and keep independent consultants to monitor and report annually from outside the project, then act promptly on their recommendations, in order to improve compliance with that plan. Works contracts had to carry provisions enforcing the environmental plan, with penalties for failure written in. The rest covered a dam safety panel and dam safety plans, periodic inspection of the dams, six-monthly reporting, a mid-term review by 30 June 2015, a procurement and financial management information system running within 45 days of the loan taking effect, operation and maintenance plans furnished to the Bank three months before each irrigation facility was finished, water user associations in each county under the water user association manual, and a programme within four months of each branch canal's completion for extending the community-driven approach beyond the demonstration areas, with Mianyang City made to fund it. The appraisal data sheet names five triggered policies: environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01), natural habitats (OP/BP 4.04), pest management (OP 4.09), involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12) and safety of dams (OP/BP 4.37). Environmental Category A.

The appraisal document of 24 April 2012 prints five legal covenants and no condition of effectiveness or disbursement. Yining Municipality had to keep an adequate organisational structure in place; carry out the environmental management plan, the resettlement action plan and the Ethnic Minority Development Plan; send the Bank six-monthly project reports; send six-monthly progress reports on how those three plans were being carried out; and send a mid-term progress report by 30 June 2015. Four safeguard policies were triggered, at Environmental Category B: environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01), physical cultural resources (OP/BP 4.11), indigenous peoples (OP/BP 4.10) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). The resettlement plan was prepared because OP 4.12 requires one where a project takes land and demolishes housing. The Ethnic Minority Development Plan came out of the social assessment and was written to make the design meet the needs of local Uygur communities. What the agreement did not carry is a sum of money. The appraisal document says RMB123.16 million was budgeted for compensation and resettlement. The Independent Evaluation Group, which read the loan agreement, records that this amount, about US$19.5 million, appears in no project cost table, and that spending on land acquisition is not mentioned in the appraisal document, the loan agreement or the completion report. The duty to carry out the plan was covenanted; the cost of doing so was never fixed in the loan documents.

Nothing particular to this project was attached to the money. The appraisal document of 15 March 2011 has a section headed loan conditions and covenants, and it says in full: effectiveness conditions, "No non-standard conditions"; covenants, standard ones relating to procurement, financial management and safeguards. The data sheet's line for effectiveness conditions reads "None." The project was Environmental Category A, and three policies were triggered: environmental assessment (OP/BP 4.01), natural habitats (OP/BP 4.04) and involuntary resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). OP 4.12 meant a resettlement plan with a resettlement policy framework had to be prepared, and it was. The completion report describes the standard reporting that went with it: interim financial reports, annual audited reports, periodic reports on safeguards implementation and regular progress reports in agreed formats, with independent consultants commissioned to monitor the social safeguards. None of it reached what happened at Sanba village. The loan closed on 31 December 2017, and in January 2018 the Bank was told that the county government had designated the Sanba resettlement site for development and that the 23 resettled households would be moved again. The arrangements that followed, Yingshang County's six-monthly reports on the resettlement housing, the provincial office's continued monitoring and a grievance mechanism, were things Anhui's project office agreed to do under a later project, the Bank-supported Anhui Rural Road Program, not conditions of this loan.

The appraisal document of 5 May 2010 records no condition of effectiveness: the line reads "Loan Effectiveness: None." There was one condition of disbursement, that subsidiary loan or implementation agreements acceptable to the Bank be signed between the districts and counties and their implementing agencies. Five implementation covenants followed: keep the Chongqing project management office and the local implementation units qualified and staffed; on-lend the loan proceeds on terms satisfactory to the Bank; provide adequate funding for counterpart requirements, debt repayments, operations and maintenance; show the Bank that a clinic met municipal standards before Bank-financed equipment was delivered to it; and hold a mid-term review. Environmental assessment, involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and safety of dams were triggered, at Environmental Category B. Six resettlement action plans were prepared under national law, municipal regulations and OP 4.12, and a consolidated plan was translated into English for the Bank's review and approval. The conformed Project Agreement for loan 7920-CN carries the duty to act on them. Chongqing had to minimise involuntary loss of shelter, productive assets, access to them, income or livelihood, and for that purpose had to implement the applicable resettlement plan in a manner satisfactory to the Bank before any works began. Where a change of design would displace more people, a new plan had to go to the Bank for review before that work started and then be carried out as accepted. Independent monitoring agencies acceptable to the Bank had to be engaged, with six-monthly reports to the Bank by 15 March and 15 September from 2011, and no plan could be modified or waived without the Bank's prior agreement. The subsidiary loan agreements had to make each implementing entity undertake to carry out its part of the works in accordance with the resettlement plan, the environmental plan and the resettlement policy framework. That is the term behind the completion report's line that external monitoring of safeguard implementation was carried out "in accordance with the legal agreements". When Tongliang's village land was compensated as a lease, the report says the arrangement was "finally corrected per the Bank requirements" at loan closing, three years after the works were finished.

The appraisal document of 25 May 2005 sets out three conditions of effectiveness: implementation agreements acceptable to the Bank between the Government and the three project provinces; execution of a tripartite arrangement by the United Kingdom's Department for International Development, the borrower and the Bank; and completion of that department's first deposit into the trust fund. Disbursement was then held back province by province: no money could be drawn for Guangxi, Sichuan or Yunnan until the province had trained the newly appointed county project office staff in the financial management manual and the Bank's financial management and disbursement procedures, satisfactory to the Bank, and Yunnan also had to prepare a training plan and operational guidelines for participatory planning acceptable to the Bank. The standing covenants required the borrower to keep the leading group and the provincial and county project offices staffed and resourced acceptably to the Bank, and the provincial offices to furnish annual action and work plans acceptable to the Bank by 31 October each year. Sichuan and Yunnan had to have a learning system in place for the full participatory approach by 31 March 2006, and each province had to carry out its participatory poverty assessments and participatory planning in accordance with the phasing plan and its guidelines, satisfactory to the Bank. Each province had to carry out the project in accordance with the project implementation manual, acceptable to the Bank. That manual is where the land rules sat: it contained the financial management manual, the environmental management plan, the overall resettlement policy framework, an ethnic minority planning framework with six development plans, and the participation, phasing and procurement manuals, and no part of it could be amended without the Bank's prior agreement. Two further covenants bound the money's use: at least half of cumulative project spending, loan and counterpart funds together, had to fall on components 2 to 6, and farmers were not to be required to contribute to cost recovery for those components. Each province also had to monitor and evaluate its own parts of the project, furnish an annual progress report under terms of reference satisfactory to the Bank by 15 April each year, and have its accounts audited and the reports sent to the Bank within six months of each year's end; the borrower owed a mid-term report by 1 September 2008. The Independent Evaluation Group records Environmental Category B and three triggered policies: environmental assessment (OP 4.01), indigenous peoples (OD 4.20) and involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12). Land taking was expected to be limited and scattered, with no physical relocation, so the framework guided planning where land was needed, and resettlement action plans were prepared for the first year's works.
